## How the guide defines it

Not addressed in guide.

## How the guide uses it

On 68 pages, and used as a leading indicator rather than as a talent inventory. The guide repeatedly reads a class ranking as a verdict on a coaching hire: Coastal Carolina's first class under Ryan Beard is called a nightmare by programme standards, North Texas's ranked better than only four programmes nationally, Nebraska's the worst in 15 years by 31 positions, Sacramento State's down 49 ranking positions year over year.

## Working definition — TTW DERIVED

The signing of high-school and transfer talent, usually referenced through a national class ranking.

## Why it matters — TTW DERIVED

In the guide's hands it is mostly evidence about the coach. A collapsing class is treated as the first visible sign that a programme is in trouble, often before the record is.

## How bettors use it in this guide

Comparatively and directionally — this year's class against the programme's own history, or against the rest of the conference. Contributors cite outside ranking services by name, 247Sports most often.

## Where it appears

pp. 28–37 for the carousel context; pp. 22–27 where class movement carries win-total bets; team pages for the individual classes.
